content: 1. The implementation guide toolkit provides detailed instructions for adapting the World Health Organization (WHO) Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) and Selected Practice Recommendations (SPR) guidance for national family planning guidelines. 2. It is essential to understand how to appropriately adapt the WHO MEC/SPR guidance to ensure alignment with national needs while maintaining adherence to WHO recommendations. 3. A decision tree can be used to determine whether adaptation or the development of new guidelines is necessary. 4. A relevant checklist should be utilized to plan the implementation of national family planning guidelines effectively. 5. Notes should be written on the checklist's suggestions and questions to ensure clarity and thoroughness in the adaptation process. 6. Modifications to the aesthetics and format of the guidance, as well as translation into local languages, are optional but can enhance usability and accessibility. 7. Tailoring the guidance to the level of the service provider may be appropriate depending on the specific setting. 8. In some contexts, it may be necessary to include additional counseling messages or clarifications to address local needs. How to Use This Tool: 9. The scientific content of the WHO MEC or SPR should generally remain unchanged when incorporated into national guidelines, as these recommendations are based on rigorous global research and review processes. 10. Omitting portions of the guidance should generally be avoided to ensure the delivery of evidence-based, high-quality standards. 11. Fidelity to the original WHO MEC and SPR guidance is critical; national family planning guidelines should adhere to WHO recommendations to maintain consistency and quality. Decision Diagrams for Development or Adaptation: 12. Decision diagrams can help determine whether recommendations should be developed or adapted, particularly in cases where: A condition of high prevalence or importance is not included in the WHO MEC. A contraceptive method not included in the WHO MEC is relevant. Existing recommendations are deficient or require supplementation. Expert opinion or other data sources are available to support changes. There is a current or potential health burden or hazard that necessitates action. The Ministry of Health (MoH) has the capacity and responsibility for translation, dissemination, and evaluation. Joint recommendations with partners are feasible. 13. If adaptation is pursued, ensure that professional translation services are used, including a review for technical accuracy. 14. Consider adapting or developing tools and source documents for providers, such as MEC wheels or summary charts. 15. Field testing adapted or developed tools among providers is recommended to ensure their practicality and effectiveness. Integrating WHO Recommendations into National Guidelines: 16. When integrating WHO recommendations, consider why a recommendation change is needed and involve relevant stakeholders, such as technical experts and working groups, to conduct systematic reviews and assess evidence. 17. Adaptations at the national level provide valuable feedback for improving and updating global guidance. 18. While WHO headquarters does not need to review or approve national adaptations, countries are encouraged to share their adaptations with WHO country and regional offices to inform future updates to global guidance. Timing and Justification for Changes: 19. Changes should be made during the exploration stage of WHO guidance implementation or during periodic updates to family planning guidelines. 20. Disseminate changes in a timely manner to ensure their impact. 21. Consider omitting recommendations only if: The medical condition has low prevalence. The family planning method is unavailable in the public sector or private sector. Country policies, priorities, or values are misaligned with WHO recommendations. 22. If a method is unavailable, include recommendations to advocate for its introduction. Additional Considerations: 23. Ensure that the WHO logo remains on WHO-based products, such as the MEC wheel. If the tool is adapted, remove the WHO logo and consider adding a local logo. 24. Adaptations should be carefully planned and executed to maintain the integrity of the original guidance while addressing local needs.
